I need to check whether permission resources are organized by organization or issue.

The bulk archive flow validates organization scope first. It deduplicates IDs while preserving order, then fetches issues including archived ones. Issues are skipped if missing or belong to another organization. Already-archived issues are left untouched. Remaining issues require permission checks against the issue resource. If any permission check fails, the entire call is rejected with a PermissionDeniedError and nothing is archived.

If all permission checks pass, every remaining issue is archived and an `issue.archived` event is emitted for each. The response returns archived and skipped IDs in first-appearance order. Skipped issues are never permission-checked.

The `findIssuesByIds` helper queries issues by organization and ID list, then fetches their labels in a separate batch.

The query intentionally omits the live predicate so archived issues are returned. Labels are included to keep Issue objects complete and consistent with `findIssueById`, even though permissions only check author and assignee. The repository header notes that `archivePatch`, `restorePatch`, and `shouldFilterArchived` should be reused rather than reimplemented.

The bulk archive flow must not call `assertNotArchived`, because that helper throws an error for already-archived issues. The file comment requiring it applies to existing functions, but bulk archive should simply skip those issues. Using the soft-delete `isArchived` helper is the correct way to identify them.

The bulk archive permission check must match the single-issue `issue:archive` check exactly. Because `assertCan` throws immediately on the first failure, a loop checking every remaining issue would abort before any archiving occurs.

The permission check will run in request order so the first failing ID triggers the rejection. Each issue will be archived by calling `issueRepo.archiveIssue`, reusing the existing single-issue archive path.

A race condition exists between reading issues and archiving them. Another process could archive an issue after the initial query but before the update. The existing single-issue archive path handles this same overwrite risk, so the bulk flow should follow that pattern.

The `issue.archived` event payload mirrors the single-issue archive format, carrying the actor envelope, issue ID, and project ID. It is emitted once per archived issue and never for skipped ones, in request order. The function returns a promise resolving to `{ archived: readonly IssueId[], skipped: readonly IssueId[] }`. The input schema accepts an organization ID and a non-empty array of up to 50 issue IDs.

The `BulkArchiveIssuesInput` type will be exported alongside existing types and imported into the service. The schema allows duplicate IDs, so deduplication is handled in the service rather than in the schema.

The implementation fetches issues by organization and ID, then splits them into skipped and to-archive lists using a Map for fast lookup. It checks permissions on all issues that will be archived before archiving any of them.

The repository is trusted to return only issues belonging to the requested organization. A cross-tenant issue would fail permission and reject the entire call. Duplicate IDs appear once in the skipped list. Archived and live issues are tracked independently in first-appearance order.

Member role has issue:archive permission via the role matrix. Admin and owner roles can archive any issue. The service correctly uses issueResource for permission checks. A concise comment will be added to match existing style. The backend file must be created with the exact exports specified.

No extra files or actions will be added. The service barrel already re-exports the new function automatically, so no explicit barrel updates are needed. Manifest and stub scripts likely do not require changes because hidden tests import these symbols directly.

I will review the issue-repository tests for style and empty inArray coverage. The Drizzle inArray query should handle branded string IDs correctly, matching existing patterns. I am also considering whether all archived issues should receive a single shared timestamp.

The repository's `archivePatch` uses a fresh timestamp on every call, so bulk archiving will naturally produce slightly different millisecond timestamps. This matches the existing single-issue behavior and is acceptable.

Events will be emitted asynchronously in request order. A failure during event emission after an issue has already been archived will leave some events missing, which is consistent with the existing sequential archive flow.

Archiving will happen before event emission. This ensures all issues are archived even if a later event fails, matching the existing single-issue sequential flow.

The implementation will archive each issue and emit its event in a single loop, matching the existing `archiveIssue` flow exactly. This preserves the expected event sequence for tests while keeping the permission check as a strict first step.

The action layer and archiveIssue service both perform permission checks.

The bulk archive service should reuse the same permission check as single-issue archiving. The action layer uses `can` with `ForbiddenActionError`, while the service uses `assertCan`. Every remaining issue must pass this identical check.

The service will use `assertCan` to throw `PermissionDeniedError`, matching the codebase's permission-denied error. Skipped IDs must not be permission-checked, so `findIssuesByIds` should be used instead of `getIssue`.

The bulk archive should not call the existing `archiveIssue` service. That would re-assert org scope, re-query issues, and duplicate permission checks. Instead, it will pre-filter out already-archived and missing issues, then call `repo.archiveIssue` directly.

All permissions must be validated before any archiving occurs. If any check fails, nothing gets archived.

The implementation will first verify every permission, then archive each issue via the repository and emit its event.

The event payload should mirror the single-archive flow exactly.

The actor envelope must use `actor.orgId` rather than `input.orgId`, since `assertOrgScope` already ensures they match.

The findUsersByIds pattern should be followed exactly.

Mirroring the findUsersByIds pattern for findIssuesByIds and related label helpers. Three edits are planned. BulkArchiveIssues will deduplicate IDs per service rules. Archived issues will be skipped before permission checks. The schema handles deduplication.

A comment matching existing function style will be added to bulkArchiveIssues. The type needs exporting from schemas/issue.ts. assertOrgScope throws TenantScopeError and must run before any issue lookups.

Cross-org IDs are skipped rather than rejected as tenant errors. The emit call will be copied exactly from single-archive logic. Archived IDs will follow the request order using ordered unique IDs.

The original issue ID will be pushed to the archived list for safety. Domain events will only emit if archiving succeeds. The new schema belongs immediately after archiveIssueSchema. The service import needs a BulkArchiveIssuesInput type.

The `isArchived` helper needs importing. The new function will be placed right after `archiveIssue`. A short doc comment will be added.

Tests should verify that archived IDs are skipped without throwing `assertNotArchived`. Mixed authorship must fail the entire call while leaving unrelated issues unarchived. Event counts and payloads need to match the archived list length. Duplicate IDs in the input must collapse to a single archived entry. The schema should reject zero or fifty-one IDs and accept one through fifty.

Non-ULID IDs must be rejected. findIssuesByIds should return empty arrays for empty inputs and include archived issues while excluding other-org rows. Labels will be included in test assertions to match existing patterns. Duplicate IDs at the repository level will also collapse to a single result.
